relations.note: Anchimalguén apparitions appear in a cave alongside imbunches; no further relationship is stated.
Anchimalguén guards a cave that also contains a Chivato Pillán.
Anchimalguén guards a cave associated with a great serpent.
Guevara conjectures Anchimalhuén as the Moon or woman of the Sun, later described as Antü's wife.
Guevara speculates Anchimalhuén represented the Moon, ordinarily called Küyen; later works conflate or separate them.
Later scholarship variously classifies Anchimallén as a Wekufü-type harmful power or comparable auxiliary.
Neuquén testimony assigns both beings similar purposes and flying nocturnal forms, without narrating a meeting.
Modern accounts say Anchimallén's ember-like or meteor-like form may be mistaken for Cherufe.
Comparative folklore likens their small humanoid forms, but records no shared episode or kinship.

relations.myth: Women travelling alone at dangerous hours
relations.note: Anchimallén and Mankián jointly appear in Norma Huentén's modern admonitory narrative.
